This letter examines the spectral efficiency of cell-free massive MIMO systems with multicarrier division duplex, considering uplink and downlink transmission modes separately. We derive closed-form expressions for the spectral efficiency of both transmission modes, showing that the system achieves full MIMO benefits, and that the downlink efficiency is 2 times higher than the uplink due to the time-reversal structure, which enables more accurate channel estimation and lower interference. Simulation results also confirm that the system's performance improves significantly with an increase in base stations and a decrease in user stations, and that the spectral efficiency of the cell-free system is significantly higher than traditional cell-based systems.

A new model of differential privacy called the shuffle model has been proposed as a solution to enhance privacy in client-server systems. By separating the data generation and analysis components, and using a secure shuffler to mix the data, this model offers enhanced privacy guarantees. However, its ability to provide strict $\varepsilon$-differential privacy guarantees is limited by the shuffler's capabilities. To overcome this, a new protocol has been developed, leveraging a novel method of analyzing random variables. By utilizing this protocol, accurate results can be obtained while maintaining strong privacy guarantees. Additionally, this protocol has been enhanced to incorporate a novel method of analyzing a mixture of random variables, and its analysis has been applied to specific shuffling mechanisms, demonstrating their efficacy.

Orthogonal Time Sequence Multiplexing (OTSM) is a communication technique that has gained attention for its ability to handle multiple signals in parallel. It works by assigning unique time sequences to different signals for transmission. Due to its structure, OTSM can be easily converted into an OFDM system format. This enables the use of efficient detection methods, such as Fast Fourier Transform-based algorithms. This paper presents a new approach to OTSM, utilizing a 2D time sequence, which can be converted into a single-dimensional sequence. This conversion can be achieved by multiplying the rows of the 2D time sequence. This new OTSM system is referred to as the 1D-OTSM system. It is found that the choice of the spreading matrix significantly affects the OTSM system's performance. A new approach to design the spreading matrix is proposed, which aims to minimize the computational complexity of the receiver. This approach involves using a Hadamard matrix as the spreading matrix. The proposed system is referred to as the 1D-OTSM-H. Simulation results have shown that the proposed OTSM-H system outperforms other OTSM systems, including OTSM-CD, OTSM-D, OTSM-V, OTSM-LH, OTSM-DH, OTSM-DH-H, OTSM-VH, and OTSM-HH, in terms of bit error rate. Furthermore, the OTSM-H system also demonstrated superior performance compared to OFDM.

This paper introduces the concept of an operator metric derived from the weighted $\ell^1$-convolution semigroup algebra, indexed by a weight function $\omega$. It demonstrates that this operator metric can be derived from both the weighted ultrametric and weight-dependent norm metrics through Banach algebra metrics.

High-speed imaging techniques have been employed to examine the behavior of liquid aluminum pools as they interact with laser beams in a conduction-mode melting process.  Pulsed laser beams create ripples on the surface of the molten aluminum pools, causing the molten metal to flow towards the laser beam, a phenomenon referred to as the Marangoni effect.  Observations indicate that the formation of ripples on the surface of the molten pools depends on factors such as laser intensity and pool size, with these factors also influencing the shape and size of the molten pools.  The movement patterns within the molten pools have been analyzed using a combination of high-speed imaging and computational models, providing a detailed understanding of the thermal energy transfer and fluid dynamics within these pools.  These findings offer new insights into the behavior of molten pools and their movement patterns, offering guidance on how to optimize the melting process for industrial applications.

This research investigates the joint design of transmit power and beamforming strategies in a wireless energy transfer system for public transport vehicles assisted by an intelligent reflecting surface. The setup includes a base station that simultaneously transmits information to vehicles and charges them using a surface that reflects energy, while a cloud-based edge server optimizes the network by considering the energy transfer and data transmission. The energy transfer process is analyzed using a time-varying channel model, and a hybrid automatic repeat request ( HARQ) mechanism is applied to improve connectivity. The base station and the SRS are treated as decision makers with conflicting interests regarding the energy transfer and data transmission. The energy transfer and data transmission are optimized by the cloud-based edge server using a game-theoretic approach. The outcome of the game is a Nash equilibrium that maximizes the energy transfer and data transmission, and a novel algorithm is developed to reach this equilibrium. The simulation results demonstrate the performance of the proposed system.

Researchers have studied the complexity of DNF and CNF formulas, but there's a gap in understanding how many of these expressions exist for each degree. Our work aims to fill this gap by providing estimated lower bounds on the number of CNF and DNF formulas of different degrees. We also explore the typical degree of random CNF and DNF expressions.

This research paper aims to develop topological methods for identifying pairs of distinct equilibrium points within a P-function framework. Our approach is founded on the principle that the index of a function with multiple equilibrium points is nondegenerate if, and only if, those points can be individually isolated. A novel application of this concept arises in coevolutionary models, where we demonstrate that the equilibrium points representing species extinction and coexistence are isolated when the system exhibits a unique stable equilibrium. Our primary contribution is a parameterized topological index, denoted by $f_{n}(I)$, which is calculated by incorporating a controlled perturbation function into the original P-function. Additionally, we derive a real-valued analogue of this index, $f(I)$, and illustrate its practical uses in identifying coexistence of species within ecological systems.

The study of strange quark stars, particularly their composition and internal structure, has significant implications for understanding the mysterious nature of dark matter and dark energy, as well as the possibility of gravitational wave detection. A novel model, incorporating temperature and magnetic field effects, has been developed to analyze quark matter under various conditions. The model's application to a system with strange quarks reveals that their interaction changes from attractive to repulsive at a critical temperature, affecting the star's structure and evolution. The impact of magnetic fields on the equation of state and thermodynamic properties of strange quark matter is also examined, along with its potential implications for the structure and evolution of strange quark stars. The model's predictions, including mass-radius and pressure-volume relationships, are used to explore the evolution of strange quark stars under different temperature and magnetic field conditions. The study's findings have implications for understanding the behavior of compact stars, particularly those with high magnetic fields, in the context of the recent rapidistic pulsar PSR J $062141.53+622735.81$ discovered in the Cygnus X-3 X-ray binary system.

A new technique in human-robot interaction, audiovisual scene understanding, can be improved by using artificial intelligence. Recent studies have developed methods to analyze audiovisual data using a unified representation, achieving better understanding of similar sounds and visuals. In audiovisual association, deep learning models have been utilized to analyze features from both audio and visuals. However, audiovisual association still faces challenges due to variations in audio and visual features, and limited datasets. To overcome these issues, recent studies have employed techniques such as cross-modal contrastive learning, cross-modal distillation, and graph neural networks. These approaches aim to enhance audiovisual association by aligning audio and visual data in a unified representation, and can be applied to various tasks such as audiovisual retrieval, classification, and question-answering. However, they require audiovisual datasets and models to be trained and tested. In this article, we discuss the recent studies on audiovisual association, and provide insights into the current findings and future challenges.

We investigate the dependability of remedies in a network consisting of linearly arranged components, each with a known and unpredictable failure rate. Remedies can be used to temporarily restore functionality to failed components. Assuming the component failure events are independent, we introduce two new metrics for evaluating the system's dependability. The first measures the system's total operational time before reaching an irreparable failure state, and the second assesses the system's likelihood of reaching a point where all components have failed. To address these metrics, we develop a dynamic programming solution for the optimal selection of activated remedies and present two heuristic algorithms that achieve near-optimal results, one of which runs more efficiently than the other according to our experimental results.

The influence of granular superconductivity on the fluctuation behavior of superconducting materials has been a topic of ongoing debate. In this study, we investigated how the superconducting critical temperature fluctuations change as the size of the superconducting nanowires decreases. Contrary to expectations, our findings reveal that the superconducting critical temperature fluctuations become more pronounced as the size of the superconducting nanowires decreases. This result is consistent with the idea that the superconducting nanowires' finite size enhances the role of granular superconductivity in critical temperature fluctuations.

We introduce a query language, TPCQ, for managing temporal information that guarantees consistent outcomes across different temporal viewpoints. TPCQ is based on a unique graph structure that combines multiple event graphs according to a specific timeline, and it supports various temporal analytics, including identifying temporal connections, discrediting invalid sequences, and applying conditional logic. The method ensures temporal consistency by linking events across event graphs, and it leverages a novel graph structure, the PCG+, to efficiently detect inconsistencies within individual graphs. The TPCQ system offers multiple optimization techniques, such as index-based lookup and summary-based verification, and it can be extended to accommodate additional temporal operators by incorporating a finite-state automaton to validate temporal constraints.

Our study explores the behavior of the free radical CH2O2+ when it interacts with Li2+ at the base of a micro-wave cavity operating at a 750 MHz frequency. The combination of microwave and magnetic fields enables the deceleration of particles in two phases: initially, Li2+ is slowed down by the microwave, followed by simultaneous deceleration using both microwave and magnetic fields that capture the radical. The observed trapping efficiency of the radical ranges from 20 to 50%.

We've developed a system to identify transient or variable sources in real-time using data from the Swift-XRT, complemented by a catalogue of persistent sources called the Living Swift-XRT Point Source catalogue. This system relies on the Subarray of the X-ray Integral Field Unit to continuously monitor the sky by taking 10-second snapshots of a 1.8 degree region. To expedite the analysis, our method relies on rapid image processing, calibration, and source detection, leveraging a combination of Python and Python-FITS (Astropy library). The system's output includes flux and error estimates for detected sources, along with a catalogue of temporary sources. To enhance efficiency, we've integrated automated periodisation and source identification, leveraging the OOPs Python library and cPlex. The system's functionality extends to Sun observation mode, allowing for Sun-flux calibration. The system's output is publicly available through a Python API, web-based visualisation, and social media platforms, with a Twitter account (@LivingSXPS). The system's functionality also encompasses the identification of short-term transient phenomena, such as solar flares, along with a web-based visualisation of temporary sources.

In the context of the spin-1/2 J1-J2 XY model on a square lattice, a unique ground state configuration, known as the plaquette valence bond (PVB) state, is found to be a possible solution. The PVB state is essentially a spin singlet formed by adjacent spins S1 and S2. By calculating the energy required to transition between the ground state and the high-temperature state, as well as the specific heat of the high-temperature state, researchers have been able to pinpoint the exact location of the phase transition. Additionally, a quantum phase transition between the ground state and the high-temperature state is found to occur at a specific point, and the presence of a critical exponent of approximately 0.125 was identified. The results of the investigation also indicate that the specific heat exhibits a characteristic peak at the high-temperature side of the transition point.

This paper introduces a new approach to breaking down international trade flows by sector and country of origin and destination. This enables a more precise analysis of the impact on international trade when one country's exports are influenced by another's. In the context of international trade, factor flows are often measured in terms of value, typically analyzed through matrices. However, this structure fails to consider the diverse origins and destinations of trade. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a panel data structure with three dimensions. It demonstrates the method's ability to accurately estimate trade volumes while minimizing errors. Using this approach, it examines trade flows among developed and developing countries, providing insights into how changes in international trade can affect specific countries. For instance, it shows that a 10% reduction in India's ability to export textiles to the US would increase India's textile exports to other developed countries by 1.6% and decrease its textile imports from China by 1.4%.

A four-dimensional non-commutative deformation of the $U(1)$-symmetric electromagnetism is constructed using a homotopy Batalin-Fradkin-Vafa construction. The 2-bracket of the deformation gives rise to a deformed $U(1)$-symmetric electromagnetism that is invariant of kinematic non-commutativity, while the $L_{\infty}$-bootstrap of the deformation's 0-bracket gives rise to a new self-interaction term of the electromagnetic potential.

The equalization problem in quantum information theory revolves around transforming an arbitrary quantum state into a known, optimal outcome, known as a reference state. In addressing this challenge, this study focuses on a specific variant known as consistent equalization, where the goal is to transfer the quantum state from one system to a reference state in the target system while implementing a predetermined unitary transformation on the initial system's environment. In the case of linear inflation, where the reference state's dimension continuously increases, it's shown that the task is achievable under certain conditions, provided that the initial quantum state is finite-dimensional. Furthermore, it's proven that the required unitary operation on the environment can be accomplished using a limited number of quantum operations, which adds to the complexity of the problem. In the context of consistent equalization, a specific measure of performance is introduced and used to derive a necessary condition for the method's success. In the case of a reference state with a constant dimension, it's demonstrated that the study's results are optimal and provide a precise solution. In addition, it's shown that the initial quantum state can be transformed into the reference state using a limited number of quantum operations, provided that the environment's unitary operation on the system is applicable.

Individuals experiencing mental health issues often have difficulty maintaining a sense of current time, which complicates their treatment and daily routines. Existing research has employed machine learning to forecast time awareness from electrodermal activity, but these models were trained on brief, static datasets that don't reflect real-world variations in mental state and daily activities. Furthermore, they were not designed to handle the long delay between when time awareness behaviors actually occur and when a model can provide a prediction. To address these challenges, we developed a wearable device that continuously monitors EDX and uses two machine learning models to predict the current time, one of which was trained using a static dataset and the other, an online model, which was trained in small increments. The online model provided a significant improvement in accuracy.

We investigate the impact of decision-making speed on complexity by analyzing a large dataset of chess games. Our findings reveal a significant correlation between decision speed and decision quality, with slower decisions leading to better outcomes in both short-term and long-term scenarios. Notably, players who prefer slower play tend to outperform their opponents and achieve better results. Furthermore, our research uncovers a relationship between decision speed, quality, and player skill level, indicating that more skilled players are capable of processing complex information more efficiently. Our study also provides insights into the optimal decision-making speed, suggesting that players who decide quickly but with lower quality decisions are less likely to succeed. Ultimately, our research provides a comprehensive understanding of the intricate relationship between decision-making speed, quality, and skill levels in complex real-world scenarios.

In cases involving automated decision-making systems that affect people's rights, legal definitions of fairness are necessary to resolve disputes arising from such systems' effects. Different approaches have been developed for fairness definitions, yet little attention has been given to the underlying assumptions of these definitions. This paper presents a framework for analyzing the underlying premises of fairness definitions, which is applied to well-known fairness definitions, including those for decision support systems and machine learning models. The analysis highlights inconsistencies in the underlying premises of these definitions, which may lead to contradictory outcomes in real-world scenarios. As such, the paper advocates for greater consideration of these premises in the development of fairness definitions, with the ultimate goal of creating a more inclusive and equitable automated decision-making system.

A theoretical model explores the process of discharging trivalent lanthanide ions in a Yb:LuVO$_4$ crystal through the interaction of a pair of spinless Majorana particles. The initial step involves the creation of a localized excited state by introducing a pair of Majorana particles into the crystal, which is then followed by the discharging process that restores the ground state through the emission of two neutrinos. The study examines the effect of external magnetic fields on the magnetization of noncollinear ground state configurations of trivalent lanathanide ions in the crystal. The discharging process is triggered by the absorption of two spin-polarized neutrinos from a source outside the crystal. The study also considers the possibility of generating a magnetic signal from the restored ground state and utilizes the parity violating magnetization to investigate this process.

Using the unitary group model and chiral effective field theory, we've studied $\Lambda^3$, $\Lambda^4$, $\Lambda^5$, $\Lambda^6$, $\Lambda^7$, $\Lambda^8$ and $\bar{\Lambda}^4$ hypernuclei in terms of strangeness, magnetic and electric isospin. We've also explored the hyperon separation energy in relation to isospin, the ratio of strangeness and isospin separation energy, the hyperon separation energy's dependence on isospin and density, and the existence of the hyperon shell gap threshold. Our analysis revealed that the predicted $A=8$ double-strangeness hypernuclei have a lower binding energy than the calculated single-strangeness hypernuclei, and the observed $A=7$ double-strangeness hypernuclei binding energy is consistent with the experimentally measured value.

Social media platforms have become essential tools for communication, however,
they pose significant risks to users' private lives. Online content is often
shared with specific individuals, yet publicly available with no security in place.
In this paper, a new social networking system is introduced that allows users to
selectively share content on a peer-to-peer basis, ensuring it remains private
until explicitly viewed by the intended parties. A decentralized framework is
proposed that leverages blockchain and gossip protocols for secure data
dissemination.

We investigate how random events, such as the merging of populations in a branching process influenced by a changing environment, are distributed over time. To establish this distribution, we first demonstrate the limits of the time at which population sizes coalesce and merge in a variable environment eventually approach zero. Next, we find the probability distribution of the times at which population sizes coalesce and merge using a renewal equation and the limits of the probabilities of various events in multiple branching processes. Finally, we demonstrate that this distribution is a Poisson point process with a specific intensity function.
We expand the Hamiltonian framework to include a countable set of spin values, enabling the derivation of uncountable Gibbs measure collections.

A galaxy's kinematic properties are crucial in understanding its overall structure and composition. Unfortunately, studies on the kinematics of galaxies within the low surface brightness regime are limited due to the difficulty of obtaining high-resolution spectra. This paper presents a catalog of 13,784 galaxies from the LAMOST-DR7 database with available high-resolution spectra and measured velocity dispersions. Velocity dispersions were calculated using cross-correlation techniques with template stars and are reported in a catalog of LAMOST-DR7 galaxies with a range of 50 to 170 km/s. This paper also explores the relationship between velocity dispersion and various galaxy properties, including luminosity, color, and Sersic index. Furthermore, the catalog allows users to access and analyze associated parameters, including velocity dispersion, galaxy luminosity, and Sersic index.

We introduce a novel method for calculating isotope shifts by combining relativistic calculations using the multireference coupled-cluster method, which considers both electron and nuclear wave functions in a 4-component Dirac framework. The method's accuracy is tested by examining the nuclear charge and neutron radius in lead, and later it is applied to study isotope shifts in indium. Specifically, we investigate the interaction between the $5^2 P_{1/2}$ state and the low-lying $5^2 S$ state in indium isotopes. The results show that including relativity and the indium's core in the calculations leads to a good agreement with the experimental data.

In this context, we explore graph states generated from a vast family of entangled states created using stabilizer operators. These graph states are uniquely defined by simple linear relationships represented by a graph's principal minors. By investigating the properties of these entangled states, we demonstrate how a specific category of graph states with restricted vertex connections can be reduced to a more limited form. Additionally, we establish a fundamental condition that determines the maximum degree of entanglement within these states and specifically shows that certain types of graph states with unique vertex connections are maximally entangled. Furthermore, we find that these maximally entangled graph states are associated with a specific category of non-bipartite graphs and provide a simplified method for representing these complex states. These results are further verified through numerical simulations demonstrating the occurrence of entanglement in these states.

A necessary condition for the existence and construction of transversals in hypergraphs is established. Specific applications of this criterion reveal its connection to a classic theorem on matchings in bipartite graphs and a long-standing problem involving the existence of 2-matchings in directed multigraphs.

In modern times, cloud services have become ubiquitous, enabling seamless access to resources on demand. Users can select from a diverse range of virtual machines tailored to specific needs, offering a range of processing capabilities. By leveraging cloud services, video producers can efficiently handle tasks such as transcoding and rendering, which are often time-consuming and require significant computational resources. However, current approaches often lead to overprovisioning and underutilization of resources, resulting in unnecessary costs. This paper presents a novel video transcoding framework that optimizes performance by identifying and exploiting opportunities for parallel processing, maximizing the capabilities of available virtual machines. By applying our framework in a real-world scenario, we demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the average cost per transcode job by 20% and underutilization of resources by 88%, ultimately leading to substantial savings.

We've discovered that in the context of perfect state transfer in graphs utilizing the quantum Ising model, intermediate discrepancies in cycle length can actually boost coherence and help achieve faster state transfer. This contrasts with the long-held belief that shorter cycles should be utilized as closer approximations to the second shortest cycle would improve efficiency. Our findings apply to both directed and undirected graphs, with directed graphs potentially benefiting from the addition of directed loops, which are analogous to negative weights, allowing perfect state transfer to be achieved.

We examine the principal energy state of the time-dependent, three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation with a high total mass under certain non-linear conditions that exceed its critical value for energy. The principal energy state is a solution with negative frequency and is characterized by a single blow-up point at a time $t=0$ and a positive frequency. Our analysis shows that, in contrast to the mass-critical case, this solution's Morse index is zero, which resolves an open issue proposed by Maialac, Spillantini, and Terracina.

This study introduces a theoretical framework that outlines the key components necessary for measuring design quality. The proposed methodology enables the calculation of design quality in various domains, including product design, packaging, and architecture, using both qualitative and quantitative criteria. The framework's primary contribution lies in its ability to set a strict threshold for Type I errors in design evaluations, where Type I errors occur when a suboptimal design is mistakenly identified as optimal. The proposed approach is adaptable to different design evaluation functions, allowing for a range of practical applications. The framework's effectiveness is demonstrated through numerical examples, which show its potential to be applied in practice, and the associated Python code is publicly accessible.

In the age of the Internet, creating immersive, interactive virtual worlds is a pressing issue. We focus on enhancing remote virtual walk-throughs with better scalability, lower latency, and more realistic graphics. Our research introduces a distributed rendering architecture that allows each client to render a local perspective and overlay semi-transparent background elements in real-time. This approach enables a more efficient use of hardware resources, while also enabling features like dynamic lighting and supporting 3D rendering of virtual objects. Our proposed architecture is demonstrated through a case study involving a virtual tour of the University of California, Santa Barbara's Architecture studios. This case study showcases the capabilities of our system in rendering realistic and interactive environments, even under the constraints of a standard home Wi-Fi connection.

This research investigates the distinction between precise human annotations and less reliable automated music tagging techniques, particularly in complex musical contexts. Through a case study of four prominent music datasets, we examine the impact of these differences on the performance of alignment systems, taking a multi-faceted approach to measure the disparity in label accuracy. By developing and testing evaluation metrics for both the tags themselves and the underlying structural elements, we aim to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the gap between human and machine label precision. Our findings are expected to inform the design of more effective evaluation methods to differentiate between alignment systems with varying levels of human involvement in the annotation process.

This tutorial delves into the realm of in-band full-duplex communication, focusing on self-interference mitigation techniques. Initially, we outline the underlying challenges and offer a detailed channel representation. Next, we present and examine two categories of interference cancellation methods - those employing channel estimation, and those that do not - to illustrate their respective strengths and limitations. Furthermore, we highlight several multiple antenna methods designed to reduce self-interference. Finally, we converge these mitigation techniques into a unified framework and identify potential research avenues for future study.

The consolidation of colloidal droplets plays a critical role in various droplet-based manufacturing techniques, including 3D printing and droplet epitaxy.  In this study, the consolidation of a droplet is mathematically modeled by analyzing the dynamic behavior of its surface.  Our findings reveal that the colloidal gel's formation results in a combination of surface bending and surface curvature or invagination.  We have derived mathematical descriptions of both surface curvature and invagination during consolidation, which are supported by experimental data obtained using optical surface profiling.  Our results show that the rate and magnitude of surface bending or invagination directly influence the final morphology of the consolidated droplet, serving as a crucial indicator of the droplet's consolidation behavior.  These findings are expected to contribute significantly to the development of droplet-based manufacturing techniques, ultimately enhancing our understanding of droplet behavior and dynamics.

A recent study of protoplanetary disks around 25 stars revealed UV emission that is likely caused by gas particles. Research suggests that the emission is often centered at the edge of the disk and can be influenced by dust particles. The study found that the UV emission is usually associated with regions of the disk that are rich in gas and has also detected Lyman-alpha emission in some disks. Analysis of the study's data suggests that the UV emission is highest in disks that are young and have a high amount of gas, and is reduced in older disks. The study's findings are consistent with theoretical models of the distribution of UV emission in disk systems.

A cutting-edge localization system is introduced for frequency-agile and wide-band arrays in millimeter wave frequencies. The system utilizes both active and passive components, and a clever algorithm to enhance the accuracy of fingerprinting in highly obstructed urban environments. The system incorporates a surface that can be adjusted and a software-defined base station, allowing it to dynamically change its transmission settings and optimize its performance. The effectiveness of the proposed system is demonstrated through both numerical and experimental evidence, showcasing its ability to achieve high localization precision, even under conditions that would typically cause significant errors.

We demonstrate that when a charged particle with initial spin interacts with electromagnetic fields, the resulting spin-orbit coupling leads to the production of twisted particles. This phenomenon is mathematically represented through the use of the Fock state $|F\rangle$. Notably, the particle's electromagnetic current and the electromagnetic fields' energy-momentum tensor are found to be connected by specific angular momenta, offering insight into the relationship between energy and angular momentum in the twisted particles' creation.

As the electric vehicle market expands, it's crucial for charging station operators to optimize their investments by attracting as many users as possible and maximizing revenue. To this end, our research explores the most effective pricing and placement strategies for DC fast charging stations serving both private and public users. We developed a model that takes into account user travel patterns, supply limitations, and market competition, allowing for the optimization of both pricing and placement. We also created a dynamic simulation model to test the success of different market approaches, specifically for electric vehicle charging operators. Our findings indicate that DC fast charging outperforms other technologies in terms of user satisfaction and revenue generation. By strategically selecting locations, operators can serve a larger customer base and increase their revenue. We propose a market segmentation approach, where operators focus on specific regions and user groups, rather than vying for a universal market. Our research suggests that this targeted approach can increase revenue by up to 20%.

An ideal tie-breaker design is a linear block design where every possible treatment comparison is represented by a specific linear combination of vectors in the design. The main focus of this study is to identify the conditions that allow an ideal tie-breaker structure to be achievable given a certain number of treatments. Specifically, it is demonstrated that an ideal tie-breaker structure can be achieved under various conditions, including when the number of treatments is one more or two less than the number of experiments, and when the number of experiments is three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine, given certain constraints are met in terms of replication and treatment arrangement. Additionally, an algorithm has been developed to create an ideal tie-breaker design from existing designs lacking a specific structure.

In the context of the N=1 superconformal theory, where superconformal group is SO(4), we examine three-point correlators involving multiplets of higher-order currents within class Ic, II, III, V, V', and VI. These multiplets are derived from superconformal representation theory and are linked to the lowest supermultiplets containing currents of different spin. By solving free theory equations, we find the three-point correlators' coefficients, which are determined by the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients of SO(4) Lie algebra and the Casimir operators' eigenvalues of superconformal group. These results can be applied to study conformal field theories with specific properties, such as N=1 superconformal field theories with SO(4) symmetry, where superconformal invariance and conformal unitarity ensure non-degenerate results.

Recent advancements in NLP have led to the emergence of a new area of research, focusing on the creation of machine instruction, which involves teaching tasks to AI models. This emerging field is of particular interest because it has implications for the broader AI community, as well as raising ethical concerns, given the potential for language-based manipulation. This study explores the dynamics of machine instruction through a unique approach, which involves children teaching AI systems in a game-like setup. By analyzing children's instructions and the AI system's responses, our research reveals that children predominantly use explicit, clear, and grammatically correct directions. However, the AI system often fails to effectively respond to these instructions, which may create confusion. Our findings have significant implications for the field of machine instruction, which relies heavily on AI systems' ability to accurately interpret language. By better understanding this relationship, we can better ensure that language models are taught in ethical and effective ways.

The article focuses on Lifelong Machine Learning Systems (LMCS), which are capable of adapting to various data patterns and adapting to new information as it becomes available. This requires systems that can process large amounts of data from diverse sources, such as structured and unstructured data like documents, videos, and audio files. To achieve this, LMCS must be flexible and learn quickly from structured and unstructured data, including adapting to feedback from users. This enables the system to provide personalized responses based on user interactions. Our vision for the future of the field is that it will involve developing systems that can seamlessly integrate and process data from multiple sources, update existing knowledge, and adapt to new information. We also anticipate advancements in the areas of meta-learning, domain adaptation, and utilizing user feedback.

In recent years, research on quantum information processing using light has experienced rapid growth. This research has primarily focused on two degrees of freedom (DOFs) - the path and polarization of light. Nevertheless, researchers have begun exploring alternative photonic DOFs, such as wavelength and orbital angular momentum (OAM). A key challenge in developing photonic quantum processing is transferring quantum information between various DOFs. This study presents a new approach that utilizes a multiport interferometer incorporating multiple OAM modes. This study demonstrates the successful transformation of quantum information between the path DOF and OAM of a quantum signal, achieved through a combination of an OAM sorter and a path-OAM interchanger. Furthermore, the study investigates the effects of losses in the OAM sorter on OAM-state fidelity, and it suggests a method to mitigate the impact of these losses. Additionally, the study's experimental results confirm that the device can efficiently transfer quantum information between the path and OAM DOFs of multiple photons, simultaneously.

We investigate the electronic properties of two different DNA models featuring misaligned structures, utilizing the tight-binding framework to examine their electronic transport.  One model incorporates a misalignment with varying potential, while the other has a misalignment with zero potential consistency.  We analyze the electronic transmission characteristics of these models by computing Green's function under non-equilibrium conditions and subsequently derive the Landauer-Büttiker current using Fermi's distribution function.  Our findings indicate that DNA structures with misaligned regions exhibit distinct electronic transport properties, with electronic conduction anomalies arising from the misaligned regions' potential characteristics.  Specifically, the model with a potential-dependent misalignment yields a current decrease with increasing wire length, whereas the model with a zero-potential misalignment exhibits a non-monotonic current behavior.  We attribute these anomalies to the electronic conduction properties of misaligned regions, with the position of the misaligned site significantly impacting the electronic transport, potentially explaining the electronic conduction anomalies observed in DNA.

In applications such as 3D multi-view registration, grouping related points together can improve the transfer of information from one view to another, especially when paired with a feature-based algorithm. This paper presents a new approach to grouping 3D point sets into partially overlapping sets of connected points, based on their proximity in 3D space, that enables the use of pair-wise registrations to achieve full registration. This method involves applying the k-means clustering algorithm to group 3D point clouds and then registering each group with each other. This approach is efficient, robust, and effective in practice, as demonstrated by experimental results on a large dataset of aerial images.

Our research examines the crystal and magnetic properties of Tb3RuO7, a compound that features Ru3+ ions in a linear chain configuration with a spin value of 3/2, and a rare-earth Terbium ion with a spin value of 9/2. By employing neutron diffraction and magnetic analysis techniques, we have identified a unique magnetic arrangement that is characterized by a partially disordered state. In this configuration, the Ru ions are aligned in a way that precludes long-range magnetic order due to the opposing effects of exchange and Zeeman interactions. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a non-uniform magnetic field that is induced by the Anomalous-Diffraction effect, and this field plays a crucial role in stabilizing the disordered state. Notably, our findings suggest that the magnetic properties of Tb3RuO7 can be manipulated by modifying its chemical composition.

This study's aim is to illustrate how specific characteristics in DC programming can be harnessed to streamline directional search within the context of optimization. Utilizing the properties of the Moreau envelope and its derivatives, we've developed a novel method to identify directions that consistently decrease the objective function in each iteration. This proposed approach is adaptable to both unconstrained and constrained optimization problems with a focus on continuous and differentiable objective functions. Our optimization method is notable for its efficiency, requiring only a single gradient evaluation per iteration without necessitating a new KKT point evaluation, thereby enabling reduced computational costs. This proposed algorithm is also free of assumptions regarding the convexity of the feasible set or the optimality criteria used for the subproblems, instead employing a highly efficient homotopy-based solution method. This solution method is a primary contribution of our work, particularly in the context of equality-constrained problems.

The D$(-1$/D$7$ intersection has a unique property, where its four-dimensional part behaves as a space with non-zero AdS radius, while its zero-dimensional part behaves as a space with non-zero conformal radius. By focusing on the four-dimensional part, we can explore the curved AdS space. Our study reveals that the D$(-1$/D$7$ intersection has characteristics of a minimal flat space, while its four-dimensional part has characteristics of a curved AdS space. Our findings suggest that the $SO(2,1)$ is compactified in a manner that is similar to a compactification of the $SO(2,1)$ with a boundary. Our study also reveals that the $SO(2,1)$ is compactified in a manner that is similar to a compactification of the $SO(2,1)$ with a boundary. The concept of Domain Clashes highlights a type of discrepancy where an action's impact is perceived from a distinct perspective, originating from a unique set of assumptions, yet the person carrying out the action operates under a different set of assumptions, resulting in a mismatch between their respective frames of reference. This theoretical framework is grounded in the work of Merleau-Ponty and draws parallels with the ideas of mutual misunderstanding in the context of embodied cognition. Through this lens, it seeks to enhance our understanding of the computational and cognitive sciences. Ultimately, the goal is to provide a fresh perspective on the nature of cognitive and social discord.

Combining the benefits of control theory and machine learning has been a long-standing goal in robotics research.  A recent example of this fusion is learning-based nonlinear model predictive control (NLMPC), which integrates deep reinforcement learning to optimize control policies.  However, traditional deep reinforcement learning methods often require a large number of expensive and costly trials to reach optimal solutions.  This paper presents a novel Bayesian controller integration (BCI) approach that utilizes established control priors to inform and refine NL-MPC's control policies.  By leveraging pre-existing control priors, BCI can achieve optimal control solutions in a significantly more efficient manner, and the proposed method has been successfully tested in a robotic context using a flexible robot arm.

Perfusion modeling through mathematical simulations is a valuable approach for studying stroke and developing effective treatments. However, accurately analyzing these models poses a significant challenge due to the inherent blurring of values caused by diffusion. To address this issue, we have developed a novel, adaptable algorithm that enhances the resolution of perfusion models, leading to more accurate results. Our algorithm demonstrates substantial improvements over traditional methods both numerically and in real-world scenarios, including the analysis of simulated and actual stroke data.

We introduce an iterative approach to beam operations that involves adjusting the beam energies using Nth-order calculations while incorporating corrections for missing physics. This method is illustrated using N=3, and it effectively maintains the process's zero-jetness state, or the condition where N-jet processes are not relevant, which is crucial for avoiding unwanted effects like power corrections and jet processes. The method is applied to a hypothetical process, e+e-→Z*, and its comparison with real-jet processes, e+e-→μ+μ− plus a jet, at the N=3 order. This method is also discussed in relation to other processes, e+e-→WW and e+2γ, at the N=3 order.

The power graph of a finite group G is defined as the set of all ordered pairs (a, b), where a and b are elements of G with a being a power of b. In this context, we explore the chordality property in the power graph of finite groups and establish specific conditions under which the power graph is chordal. Additionally, for each known chordal power graph in the past literature, we verify the validity of these conditions. Furthermore, we show that certain families of groups, such as the cyclic groups of order n, the symmetric groups of order n, the alternating groups of order n, the extraspecial p-groups of exponent p and order p^k, and the Frobenius groups with p^2, do not meet the chordality criteria for their power graphs.

In target source separation, a fundamental challenge in signal processing, the objective is to isolate a specific signal from a mixture of sounds. This problem is often approached as an optimal source identification issue, in which a signal source is best matched to a given audio mixture. Current solutions, however, rely on a flawed premise that the signal representation can be fully captured by a predefined set of basis vectors. Real-world audio signal characteristics frequently contradict this assumption, necessitating the incorporation of additional parameters to accurately represent the signal. This research introduces a new approach to source identification that trains a signal representation model to optimize its performance on unseen audio samples. By leveraging the flexibility of neural networks, this model can adapt its representation to better align with the characteristics of unseen audio sources. Empirical results on a variety of audio tasks demonstrate that this model can effectively learn a signal representation that is well-suited to the separation of unseen audio sources.

This study delves into the concept of coherence within the framework of quantum observations. Building on previous findings, we established a clear definition of observationally coherent states in relation to a specific set of quantum states. We demonstrated that a subset of these states is necessary for this definition to hold. Two key properties were proven to be essential: first, a state being observationally coherent implies it is accessible by a single observation; second, a product of two observationally coherent states results in a state that is both the result of single observation and maintains coherence. Furthermore, we explored the properties of a new coherence matrix, derived a general formula for its entries, and derived a comprehensive condition for a state to be observationally coherent.

displayed type C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in various outbursts. A study
of the outbursts in 2009, 2014-2015, and 2017 revealed type C QPOs. The team
investigated the correlation between the QPOs and the outbursts' evolution, and
also examined the QPOs' connection to the accretion flow. They discovered that

corona's size, and that it's related to the accretion rate.

Government services are shifting online, creating a pressing need for reliable and secure digital interactions between citizens, businesses, and government agencies.  Public services like filing tax returns, renewing licenses, and making medical claims require precise and timely information, which can only be guaranteed through a robust and secure electronic system.  To address this need, we have developed a comprehensive QA system grounded in semantic foundations, utilizing a combination of public domain resources.  This system prioritizes accessibility, reliability, and scalability, and is adaptable for a wide range of public services.  By drawing on these principles, we have created a scalable and accessible public domain QA system, suitable for a variety of public services.

Recent advancements in the GlueX experiment have provided new insights into the existence of glueballs and lightest hybrid mesons, represented by the $q\bar{q}g$ system where $q$ is a light or heavier quark. The current study presents preliminary findings on the production of hybrid mesons containing the bottom quark within the framework of the non-relativistic quark model and Regge phenomenology.

Determining the smallest k-sized dividers, all of which are distinct and start on
the left, for extremely large values of k is an extremely complex task. In this
study, a new approach to identifying all the dividers, up to the size of k, is
presented. This new method enables us to set a predetermined limit on the
number of dividers, all of which are less than or equal to the size of k. By
setting a specific value for k, we can make the new method more efficient. In
addition, this approach has a potential application in graph theory, where it
can be used to identify all the dividers of a tree with a specified number of
vertices. The proposed method consists of two main components, a new data
structure called the Tree-Divider Table and an algorithm to construct it, as
well as an algorithm to identify and construct all the dividers, up to the size
of k.

We have identified a previously unobserved connection between certain types of
explosive astrophysical events, including supernovae and supernova-like events,
and the fading of Balmer-line-emitting nuclei in previously star-forming galaxies.
The connection involves a pattern of activity that typically begins with a
supernova-like event, followed by a sequence of luminous transient events,
ultimately resulting in the emergence of a supernova. Our analysis of
near-infrared data from 12 previously star-forming galaxies has revealed that
these transients are associated with the remnants of dormant nuclei, a
phenomenon that is linked to the process of nuclear starburst cessation.
Our findings suggest that these transients may be a previously unrecognized
indicator of supernova activity in the centers of galaxies.

In reconfigurable wireless networks, radio frequency (RF) chains can be allocated to user connections in a highly flexible manner. This allocation can be optimized to meet specific quality of service requirements, but is typically done using a complex, non-differentiable approach that involves integer programming. To address this challenge, we have developed a novel scheduler that uses a performer-critic learning framework to dynamically allocate RF channels in real-time. Our method leverages the strength of both integer programming and deep learning, and is capable of solving the scheduling problem in the same time it takes for a standard solution, with a computational complexity of O(n^3). We have tested our method in a simulated 5G network and it outperforms other approaches, achieving higher quality of service and lower power consumption, as well as lower latency.

The integration of artificial intelligence in machine translation has accelerated,
yet a crucial component remains unexploited - feedback from human post-editors.
This phenomenon occurs due to a lack of awareness about the benefits of a distinct
evaluation framework tailored for post-editing purposes. In this study, we propose
a novel, granular assessment of machine translation output, which is compatible
with human post-editing tasks. We also introduce an enhanced version of a
groundbreaking word-level evaluation metric, by addressing its initial drawbacks.
The assessment can be utilized to pinpoint areas for improvement in MT systems,
and our updated method exhibits superior correlation with human post-editing time.

We investigate how well certain spacetime metrics can be inferred from event horizons of Kerr--de Sitter black holes, using a method that involves a vector field and its circularity condition to estimate the cosmological constant. By establishing an isometric mapping between any given spacetime and a reference spacetime of the same type, we aim to find a vector field that is static in the reference spacetime but dynamic in the actual spacetime, and whose circularity condition can be used to calculate the area ratio between the two event horizons. This calculation yields an expression for the area ratio in terms of the cosmological constant, which can be confirmed through numerical comparisons. Furthermore, we demonstrate the implications of this method for its potential applications in cosmology.

In the field of astrophysical fluid dynamics, particularly in numerical relativity, obtaining accurate results for simulations is crucial due to the potential to analyze actual astrophysical events. Relativistic hydrodynamics plays a significant role in these simulations, and obtaining precise outcomes is vital. A new set of accurate numerical solutions has been developed for relativistic shock waves, and the process of verifying these solutions has revealed a systematic error in previously calculated solutions for a particular type of shock wave, with the error increasing as the dynamic importance of the relativistic effects grows. The investigation identified the source of the systematic error as linked to the method of discretizing the temporal derivative within the relativistic Euler equations. A new method of discretizing the temporal derivative has been developed, which has been shown to produce accurate results for all types of shock waves, and the corresponding Fortran code is available for open-source access.

Using the BaBar experiment's data, we conducted an amplitude analysis on the decay products of several $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ mesons, specifically those that decay into a $K^0_{\rm S}$ meson and a $D^{*}$
meson, to determine the decay properties. The analysis revealed that the observed states are consistent with being pure $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ and $D_{s2}^*(2573)^+$ resonances, and our findings confirm a significant mass difference between the two states. The calculated helicity amplitudes also showed that the states exhibit a high degree of helicity suppression.

This study aims to showcase the fractal polynomials' versatility by demonstrating their application on the Sierpiński triangle. We initially outline the underlying concepts of fractal polynomials and present an overview of the Sierpiński triangle. We then explore the properties of continuous functions defined on the Sierpiński triangle within the context of fractal polynomials, examining functions that map the triangle into itself and those that map the triangle to a subset of the triangle. We also investigate Fractalets, a specific class of functions that map points to points, and derive estimates for the Hausdorff and Minkowski dimensions of their images under fractal polynomials. Furthermore, we establish a result demonstrating that the image of the Sierpiński triangle under these functions possesses upper Minkowski dimension less than 2.

Visual information inquiries such as "Where is the Eiffel Tower located?" or "What is a panda's diet?" typically involve questions with a specific context. Developing a question answering system capable of generating visual inquiries alongside their corresponding images is a challenging task. We introduce the concept of "visual directing image" and propose methods to train a model that creates visual inquiries directly from input queries without relying on extensive training data. We also present a new dataset called "VisualIQ" comprising 1,000 question-image pairs collected from the MS COCO dataset, utilizing a novel data collection method. Our model, designed to generate visual inquiries, achieves a 0.76 Pearson correlation coefficient, indicating its ability to accurately predict the type of image that would respond to a given query.

We examine the hypothesis that supernova explosions within dark matter halos contribute to the transformation of their density profiles from a cusp-shaped structure to the characteristic NFW shape through a multi-phased, self-sustaining process. We analyze the stability of this process by analyzing the interplay between supernova feedback and dark matter core collapse within cusp-shaped halos. We find that the supernova rate of energy injection is not a constant, but rather is influenced by the halo's density profile and the supernovae's rate of occurrence, leading to a potential instability in the SN feedback due to the halo's varying mass accretion rate. Furthermore, our results suggest that, in the early universe, cusp-core transformations are unlikely to occur as a result of SN feedback.

This research aims to eliminate higher-order terms from modal logic formulas in such a way that they remain satisfiable under the Kripke frame structure. The method involves transforming higher-order terms into modal logic expressions by utilizing the properties of the modal logic's semantics. This process is facilitated by the introduction of a new concept known as the satisfiability degree of a formula. The research demonstrates a method to transform any higher-order term into an equivalent expression that has a lower satisfiability degree. The research also presents a new technique for reducing the satisfiability degree of a formula by eliminating higher-order terms. The method is applied to modal logic with the 'next on the path' operator, modal logic with the 'after' relation, and an arbitrary relation algebra that includes an 'after' component. The research further shows how to apply this technique to modal logic with the 'after' operator to make it expressively complete with respect to the class of relation algebra extensions containing an 'after' relation and comply with the principle of prefix-mover, a property that has been shown to facilitate the verification of temporal properties.

A $k$-order replicator equation is a linear differential equation with $k$-order terms and $k$ is an integer greater than or equal to $1$. This type of equation is used to model the evolution of frequencies in an $N$-dimensional simplex when a population adapts according to a function with three parameters: selection, mutation, and competition. This paper explores the long-term behavior of $k$-order replicator equations in two scenarios: one with a mapping that maintains its order, and another with a mapping that does not, but has a specific property. We find that when the mapping retains its order, the only stable solutions to the equation are the equilibrium points of the base $1$-order replicator equation. This finding holds regardless of the mutation rate. By contrast, when the mapping does not preserve order, the base mapping is not stable, and the equilibrium points of the base equation may not be the only stable solutions. This result, in turn, implies that replicator equations with a mapping that maintains its order do not exhibit any pattern of long-term growth. This contrasts with the case of $0$-order replicator equations, where the existence of non-equilibrium stable solutions is possible.

We investigate the performance of a class of tree-based, stochastic regression methods that utilize random data points at each node to determine the optimal child node. By employing a Gaussian approximation technique, we establish that the differences between predicted and actual values exhibit consistent normal distributions and establish specific limits on the rate at which these discrepancies accumulate. This analysis is then applied to create enhanced methods for choosing optimal child nodes, based on quantiles, and to develop more robust splitting criteria, leveraging the calculated means and variances.

The growing demand for electric vehicle (EV) charging is significantly impacting distribution systems due to the large number of charging stations and their considerable influence on voltage. A new, decentralized strategy for EV charging management in unbalanced distribution networks is presented in this research, where each charging station is viewed as an independent variable source. A communication-restricted-ADMM-based framework is developed to effectively balance the power exchange between charging stations and the main grid on the secondary voltage level. A comparison of the proposed approach with a centralized optimization method reveals its potential to significantly reduce the voltage deviation and power imbalance in the distribution network.

To determine the crystal and electronic properties of $SmFeO_3$ at different temperatures, researchers utilized first-principles calculations while considering lattice vibrations through the use of the quasi-harmonic approximation. The findings show that $SmFeO_3$ maintains a distorted perovskite structure at all investigated temperatures, whereas its elastic properties remain unchanged across temperatures. The calculations indicate that $SmFeO_3$ exhibits stability, and its elastic constants suggest it is ductile. The temperature dependence of lattice parameters and bulk modulus was found to be in line with experimental data, and the material's thermal expansion was found to be anisotropic. The calculated band gap and optical band gap predictions suggest that $SmFeO_3$ is an n-type semiconductor, whereas its optical properties show that the material absorbs light in the visible region but is transparent in the infrared and UV regions.

The intricate and diverse mechanisms of the human body's microbiome are a far cry from our current understanding of the human genome. Investigating the molecular processes within bacterial cells, researchers gain insight into fundamental biological mechanisms and their role in shaping human health. This knowledge can unlock innovative therapeutic approaches to address a range of diseases related to microbial imbalance. A key factor contributing to our progress is the development of techniques to chemically dissect complex biological pathways within bacterial cells. This breakthrough has enabled the analysis of key biological processes, including the synthesis of essential compounds, the regulation of cell division, and the repair of damaged DNA. Furthermore, the intricate interactions between the human microbiome and its constituent bacteria have been found to play a vital role in human health. This complex interplay involves cross-kingdom signaling, the regulation of cell cycle progression, the inhibition of cancer, and immune system modulation. The discovery of novel small molecules in human microbiome has also revealed new avenues for drug development. This review aims to provide an in-depth examination of the current state of knowledge, highlighting key areas of research and pinpointing the specific bacterial pathways that have been studied.

Achieving a balance between energy efficiency and maintaining a healthy indoor environment in buildings involves precise management of ventilation. Researchers have developed data-driven models that capture the dynamics of building ventilation by identifying key relationships between input variables and performance metrics. These models have been successfully applied in various contexts, but their accuracy often declines when applied to new scenarios due to overfitting. To address this limitation, a new approach is introduced, which integrates genetic algorithms with a conventional regression model, enabling the optimization of ventilation dynamics without compromising accuracy. By jointly refining the model and experimental settings, this approach enables automatic adaptation to different operating conditions, thereby enhancing its accuracy and transferability. Case studies demonstrate that this method outperforms traditional regression-based approaches in terms of predictive accuracy and generalizability.

We have analyzed the optical photometry of the extremely powerful transient, SN 2017gci, which was classified as a super-luminous supernova of the "blue-excess" type. Our research indicates that the SN was formed through a pair of merging stars, with a compact object and a red supergiant, and that the SN's outer layer was composed of a hydrogen-rich material with a high mass loss rate. The SN's brightness curve suggests that the SN's outer layer was ejected at a high velocity, similar to a pair of similar SNs observed in 2018. Our research indicates that the SN's outer layer was composed of a hydrogen-rich material with a high mass loss rate, and that the SN's brightness was influenced by a pair of factors: the SN's outer layer's high mass loss rate and the SN's inner layer's moderate opacity. The SN's inner layer's moderate opacity was likely caused by a pair of different processes, either a pair of different chemical elements or a pair of different molecular elements. Our research indicates that the SN's inner layer's moderate opacity played a significant role in the SN's brightness. A new quantum model has been developed to predict the magnetic behavior of two-dimensional materials with a single magnetic domain. At the atomic level, this model takes into account the unique spin properties of magnetized electrons and the interaction between nuclear spins and magnetic texture. By analyzing the resulting equations, we discovered that the long-term stability of magnetic domains is influenced by the distribution of nuclear spins and the magnetic structure of the material. We also showed that the domain wall energy is directly linked to the distribution and magnetic properties of the domain walls. Notably, our model reveals that the domain wall energy is highest when the magnetic structure and nuclear spin distribution meet specific criteria. Furthermore, our research demonstrates that the magnetic behavior of the domain walls can be manipulated by controlling either the magnetic structure or nuclear spin distribution, offering potential avenues for creating novel materials with desired magnetic properties.

A recent advancement in Natural Language Generation (NLG) is the development of visually-enriched response systems. These models are designed to incorporate visual information in response to a user query. A significant challenge in this area is determining the optimal level of visual detail to incorporate in a response. This decision is closely related to the concept of visual awareness, which refers to the extent to which a model is able to benefit from visual information. Our research proposes a new NLG approach that explicitly addresses the issue of visual awareness by deciding whether to incorporate visual information in a response. This decision is based on the level of visual awareness, which is determined by the model at training time. Our approach achieves a higher average global metric performance compared to the current state-of-the-art model.

Most deep learning applications in computer vision rely on complex neural networks, whose workings remain unclear due to the black-box nature of their architecture and parameters. To combat this issue, researchers employ visualization techniques called 'attribution' methods to understand how specific input elements affect the outcome of a classifier. These methods, though numerous, are often evaluated solely through user studies. To address this gap, our research introduces a systematic approach that combines both user studies and automated metrics to comprehensively assess these methods. Through this investigation, we discovered that different evaluation methods yield conflicting findings regarding the performance of various attribution techniques, and consequently, we recommend selecting a technique that aligns with the desired criterion.

We're investigating wormholes that aren't symmetrically reflected and have multiple shadows. Specifically, we're looking at non-symmetric thin shells in Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström space-times with two types of models: one with a non-constant curvature and one with constant curvature across all points. Our goal is to determine the conditions under which these shells are stable, taking into account the pressure inside the shell. We've developed a linear stability theory that considers small disturbances in Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström space-times. Applying this theory to our two space-times, we've found the conditions under which the shells are stable in all cases. Interestingly, we've discovered that the constant curvature model is stable under the same conditions as the non-constant curvature model. Our results also highlight the importance of pressure in maintaining stability in these complex systems.

Consider a sequence of $n$ independent random variables with identical mean $\mu$ and a common variance $\sigma^2$. Focusing on the tail behavior of these variables when summed in an alternating manner, we find that a random subset of these variables chosen at random plays a significant role. The method of "random strides" is an extension of previous work by Gao, Rinaldo, and Singer, applied to the context of random walks. The application of the central limit theorem to the sum of these variables, along with the law of large numbers, demonstrates that a limiting random walk can be accurately represented by a Brownian bridge, with a corresponding variance that is determined by the variance of the sum of coefficients from a specific permutation matrix. The connection between this variance and the entropy of the permutation matrix is established, with implications for the distribution of the random walk's path. The analysis further reveals that the distribution of the random walk's path is characterized by its Lévy metric, with a corresponding relationship to the entropy of the permutation matrix. The results are also applicable to the context of permutations, with applications to the distribution of the number of descents in random permutations, as well as the $k$-th descent of a random permutation, for any positive integer $k$.

Trimer shields, consisting of three spin-1/2 edges, have been predicted to have a gapless ground state according to the conformal field theory, yet experiments have shown otherwise. Theoretical studies of these trimer shields have been limited due to the lack of a known exact ground state. In this work, we introduce a new approach to study the trimer shield using a combination of exact diagonalization and matrix product state methods, including the application of the density matrix renormalization group. Our approach reveals a variety of complex phenomena, including phase transitions, topological orders, exotic ground states, and quantum entanglement entropy, for various configurations of the trimer shields on a triangular lattice. We have identified twenty unresolved questions that need to be answered, for example, whether the uniform or zigzag trimers exhibit quantum phase transitions, what topological order is observed in the honeycomb region, and what kind of phase transition occurs in the square region. The answers to these questions will require further theoretical studies and could be verified experimentally using a combination of exact diagonalization and numerical renormalization group.

This paper addresses the challenge of domain shift, where the distribution of a dataset changes over time. To address this problem, we have developed an innovative method for creating classifiers that accurately predict the membership of a test sample in a dataset, regardless of its actual distribution. Our approach is grounded in the concept of the Fr\'echet mean and its optimal transportation counterpart. Specifically, we have derived a novel, nonparametric classifier known as the Sample-and-Reciprocal-Point (SR-Point) classifier, which uses the Fr\'echet mean and its optimal transportation counterpart to classify test samples. Our proposed classifier offers several advantages, including its non-parametric nature, ease of interpretation, and the ability to detect whether a test sample belongs to the original dataset. Comprehensive experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed SR-Point classifier in addressing the problem of domain shift, with promising results.

This paper introduces a novel approach to automobile pose estimation and 3D reconstruction from stereo images. The central aspect of the proposed method lies in incorporating a category-specific automobile model into the process, allowing the model to utilize prior knowledge of the automobile category to enhance model flexibility. The proposed method involves two main stages: model fitting and 3D reconstruction. In the model fitting stage, a parametric model is used to represent an automobile category, and a non-rigid registration technique is used to estimate the parameters of the model. In the 3D reconstruction stage, a P3D algorithm is used to estimate the 3D coordinates of automobile components. The proposed approach demonstrates improved performance in terms of accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods through experiments on a comprehensive dataset of automobile images.

We've developed an innovative method for constructing query graphs that can handle complex questions in knowledge graphs. This approach involves selecting a subset of possible answers based on given queries and identifying relevant information in the graph through local patterns and broader connections. To achieve this, our method is divided into two stages. In the first step, it identifies potential matches by analyzing individual components of the query. In the second step, it examines these matches to determine which ones are relevant and add relevant information to the query graph. This process is repeated in an iterative manner until all relevant information has been added to the query graph. To optimize this process, our method uses a process called sketching and filling. In the initial iteration, it selects a representative sample of possible answers and adds them to the query graph as a sketch. In subsequent iterations, it expands on this sketch by identifying related matches and adding them to the query graph. This approach is efficient and scalable, making it suitable for complex questions in knowledge graphs. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This paper's primary objective is to provide a foundational overview of polynomial compositions and their relationship with monoid realms, highlighting novel applications within polynomial equations. We will delve into the distinct characteristics of polynomial compositions, their associated properties, and their general characteristics as well as their special cases. Moreover, the connections between polynomial compositions and monoid realms are explored, along with relevant corollaries. Notably, the study will reveal that polynomial compositions possess unique features distinct from those of standard polynomial multiplication.

The growing interest in graph stream processing has led to the development of
new algorithms for analyzing dynamic graphs.  However, the standard methods for
identifying entities in these graphs, such as the de-duplication method used
in graph matching, are unsuitable for processing streaming graphs.  This research
investigates the application of de-duplication techniques developed for
static graphs to streaming graphs, and compares their performance using a novel
streamlining approach.  The experiments conducted on real and simulated data
involve various configurations, and the results show that a simple, pre-set
algorithm performs better than more complex ones, and that the performance of
all methods can be improved by incorporating additional data.
